A1.justification: Both complete 26-page PDFs describe the same REPBEND work. Text extraction and visual comparison support matching the methods, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–B without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original jailbreak, over-refusal and capability evaluations in Section 4, plus ablations, activation analyses and generated-response examples in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical evaluations and analyses, including the numerical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, its four loss terms, LoRA updates and representation targets are unchanged. Section 3 revises the explanation of representation bending without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WildGuardMix, WildJailbreak and UltraChat training data and retain all jailbreak, over-refusal, capability and appendix test scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments. Both retain TA, NPO, RMU, CB and public safety-tuned models, alongside the appendix comparisons involving SFT, DPO, WHP, Safety Prompting and FUDGE.

E3.justification: The models, sample sizes, training budgets, layer selections, metrics, attack procedures and evaluators in Section 4 and Appendix A are unchanged. Appendix analyses also retain their configurations.

E4.justification: Both retain the loss-weight and layer ablations in Figures 5–7, activation and Logit Lens analyses, additional jailbreak tests, and generated-response cases. The redrawn Figure 1 remains a conceptual illustration.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests; the random-sampling descriptions and sensitivity-curve reporting also match.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings and generated examples are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains REPBEND's total average ASR of 3.25% for Mistral and 3.13% for Llama3.

T1.justification: The objective in Algorithm 1, representation-difference definitions and transformer-block equations are unchanged. The revised cosine-similarity explanation adds no mathematical definition, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: activation-steering-inspired fine-tuning, up to 95% ASR reduction, preservation of usability and capabilities, and applicability across architectures.

C2.justification: v3 foregrounds separation of safe and unsafe representations, but that interpretation already appears in v2's Section 4.6 and Figure 4. The refusal-alignment explanation and limitations concerning harmful retraining, tuning sensitivity, generalization and garbled outputs remain.

D1.justification: Dataset construction, LoRA settings, loss weights, hyperparameter searches and implementation disclosures are unchanged. Both retain the same hardware and computing-time information in Appendix B.9 and the same code, model and data access links.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and related-work discussion are unchanged. Positioning relative to activation steering, unlearning and safety representation engineering is retained.

P1.justification: Section 3 rewrites the overview and loss explanations to emphasize representation-space separation, removes repetition and cleans up phrasing. Figure 1's caption is expanded; section organization and nearly all remaining prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces the unsafe-to-safe arrow illustration with an explicit before/after depiction of intertwined and separated representation spaces. The author block, Algorithm 1 and appendix Figure 9 have small layout adjustments; result tables and other plots are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The redesigned Figure 1 and revised Section 3 explain the intended separation more clearly and align the introductory account with the existing Figure 4 analysis. This modestly improves exposition; the method, empirical evidence, reproducibility information and limitations are unchanged.
